title: Stream handshake + snapshot playbook (WIP)
body:
Context and intent:
This doc is a pragmatic product playbook for adding a resumable streaming handshake and lightweight snapshotting mechanism to the Hosted API streaming surface. Target audience: SDK engineers, product managers for hosted API, runtime engineers. This is intentionally practical: small API changes + SDK ergonomics + rollout + safety nets.

Why this matters (problem statement):
- Customers embed streaming LLM calls in UIs with optimistic updates and they need: uninterrupted UX across flaky mobile networks, predictable semantics for tool-calls during reconnects, and compact resumable state to avoid re-sending large prompts or re-running expensive tool steps.
- Current streaming semantics (one-off SSE/gRPC stream per request) make reconnects destructive: client must restart from scratch or rely on application logic to de-dupe tool invocations.
- Tool calls (external action requests) are particularly sensitive: duplicates can cause side-effects (charges, orders, emails).

Primary goals:
1) Provide a minimal handshake protocol: enables resumable session negotiation (session id, last-ack token, optional snapshot token).
2) Support succinct server-generated snapshots of the runtime state (KV-like prefix cache + tool-call checkpoint) that clients can request on reconnect to resume without re-running tool calls.
3) Define safe semantics for tool-calls during reconnects: idempotency tokens, preflight/commit pattern, and explicit commit acknowledgement in the stream.
4) Offer SDK ergonomics: resumable iterators and automatic backpressure primitives so app developers get correct-by-default behavior.

Non-goals:
- Full ACID transactions across tool providers (out of scope).
- Complex long-lived session storage with unbounded retention (we'll use TTL-ed snapshots and opportunistic pruning).

Proposed high-level approach:
- Add a short-lived session handshake step before streaming content: client->server: OPEN {session_id?, last_seen_seq?, snapshot_token?}. Server replies OPEN_ACK {session_state: fresh|resumed|replay_required, current_seq, snapshot_available?}.
- Snapshots are opaque small JSON blobs produced by the model-serving layer containing: model_prefix_hash, kv_prefix_snapshot (truncated), pending_tool_calls (id + status), sequence_cursor. Snapshots are thrifted to object storage and referenced by short snapshot_token (base62 handle). Snapshot TTL: default 24 hours.
- Tool calls use a two-phase lightweight protocol for safety across reconnects: CALL_PREPARE (client or model asks runtime to prepare invocation, runtime emits tool_call_id), CALL_EXECUTE (runtime calls external tool once), CALL_COMMIT (runtime/client signals safe-to-acknowledge). On reconnect, server replay can detect CALL_PREPARE without EXECUTE and either re-run EXECUTE (if idempotent) or report to client for manual reconciliation.

API sketch (stream-level envelopes) - informal:
- Transport: existing streaming HTTP+SSE or HTTP/2 gRPC preferred. New top-level envelope types on the stream: OPEN, OPEN_ACK, SNAPSHOT_CHUNK, TOKENIZE_PROGRESS, OUTPUT_CHUNK, TOOL_PREPARE, TOOL_RESULT, TOOL_COMMIT, HEARTBEAT, CLOSE, ERROR.
- Each envelope includes: seq (monotonic int), session_id, timestamp, and an opt "ref" field to correlate tool calls.

Sample minimal OPEN sequence:
Client -> server:
{ "type": "OPEN", "session_id": "user-82-2026-02-19-...", "last_seen_seq": 410, "snapshot_token": "sXp2tZ" }
Server -> client:
{ "type": "OPEN_ACK", "session_state": "resumed", "current_seq": 412, "snapshot_available": true }
(If server says resumed & snapshot_available, it will stream a small SNAPSHOT_CHUNK next.)

Snapshot design notes:
- Snapshots are intentionally small (aim < 6KB compressed) - contain a model_prefix_hash, last user prompt suffix used for KV cache, user-visible last partial output and a list of pending tool call ids with lightweight metadata (id, provider_hint, idempotency_key).
- Server retains snapshot blobs for 24–72 hours depending on SLA tier. Dedicated customers can opt-in for longer retention.
- Snapshots are cryptographically signed by control plane keys to avoid tampering in private deployments.

Tool-call safety and idempotency patterns:
- For any tool that triggers real-world side effects, the recommended integration pattern is: client provides idempotency_key when initiating actions through the model; runtime emits tool_call_id and persists it; tool provider should support idempotency_key semantics or runtime will wrap provider calls with a proxy that enforces idempotency (best-effort).
- Preflight/commit flows: when model requests an action, the runtime emits TOOL_PREPARE with idempotency_key and awaits TOOL_EXECUTE result from runtime->provider. After TOOL_EXECUTE succeeds, model runtime streams TOOL_COMMIT (or TOOL_CANCEL) to mark finality. If a reconnect occurs between EXECUTE and COMMIT, server can re-send TOOL_EXECUTE result or mark as pending for client reconciliation.

SDK ergonomics (developer experience):
- High-level goals: no footguns, minimal surface area, fail-safe defaults. SDKs should provide:
  * ResumableStreamingSession() object that hides OPEN/OPEN_ACK and manages snapshot requests automatically.
  * Async iterator API: for await (const chunk of session.stream()) { } where chunk types are unified objects with .type and helpers like chunk.isToolCall(), chunk.asText().
  * Automatic backpressure token: SDK throttles send rate by default and exposes a low-level send(token) if apps need tighter control.
  * Tool-call helpers: sdk.prepareToolCall({provider, idempotencyKey, meta}) returns a Promise that resolves when the runtime has executed or when the SDK has flagged a tool as pending post-reconnect. The SDK surfaces a reconcile() hook so apps can show UI when an action might have been executed but not committed.
  * Snapshot caching: SDKs maintain a local ephemeral snapshot cache keyed by snapshot_token to accelerate reconnects for mobile clients. Cache eviction follows server TTL.

Telemetry, observability, and SLOs:
- Track metrics per session: handshake_latency, resumed_rate (fraction of OPENs that resumed), average_snapshot_size, snapshot_retrieve_latency, pending_tool_calls_per_session, duplicate_tool_execute_count (top-warning signal).
- Logging: every tool_call_id and idempotency_key pair must be recorded in trace logs with lifecycle events (prepare, execute, commit, cancel).
- Alerts: spike in duplicate_tool_execute_count or high replay_required rate should alert infra and product.

Rollout and migration plan (practical):
- Phase 0 (canary SDK): expose feature behind a feature flag in SDK and runtime; opt-in by default for internal beta customers. Collect telemetry, watch duplicate tool executions. Timeline: 2–4 weeks.
- Phase 1 (wider beta): enable for 20% of hosted API traffic, retain snapshots for 24h, provide dashboard for resumed_rate and duplicate_tool_execute_count. Timeline: 4–8 weeks.
- Phase 2 (general availability): enable by default, increase snapshot retention per tier, add admin controls in Console (snapshot retention, snapshot purge, session inspection). Timeline: 8–12 weeks post-beta.

Security and compliance notes:
- Snapshots might contain prompt fragments. Default behavior: redact PII by running snapshot through privacy scrubber before persistence. Provide opt-out for Dedicated/Private customers to skip scrub (customer responsible).
- Snapshots are encrypted at rest and signed. For Private deployments, snapshots can be stored in customer-managed buckets.

Open questions / risks (short list):
- How big will snapshots realistically get for typical apps? We should run a small experiment to capture KV prefix sizes across real workloads.
- Tool provider idempotency: runtime wrapping improves safety but introduces latency/cost; need to define a policy and opt-in behavior.
- UX surface for partial-tool states: who reconciles? App or operator? Need to document patterns and provide SDK helpers.

Appendix: example stream envelope (single-line JSON for readability)
{
  "seq": 521,
  "type": "TOOL_PREPARE",
  "session_id": "s-usr-82-2026-02-19",
  "ref": "tool-34",
  "payload": { "provider": "calendar-v2", "idempotency_key": "abc-123", "intent": "create_event", "meta": { "tz": "PST" } }
}

Next steps (owners):
- Product (Asha): finalize API contract with runtime by 2026-03-05.
- Runtime (Ethan + Ravi): prototype snapshot blob format, measure size distribution, implement snapshot short-term store.
- SDK (Marina + Claire): prototype ResumableStreamingSession in JS and Python, initial ergonomic tests in two internal apps.
- Observability (SRE): add metrics and tracing hooks for tool_call lifecycle.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a tiny binary delta format for snapshots to support ultra-low bandwidth mobile restores.
- Consider introducing an optional "commit-lease" TTL for tool_commit: if not committed within X seconds, auto-mark pending and notify app via SDK.
- Provide a console view that shows a compact timeline for a given session id (handshake -> snapshot -> tool events -> output).

References and inspiration:
- Our prior streaming work on typed envelopes (see linked artifacts).
- Mobile app designers at Beta customers asked for reconnect resume in chat with tool links.

This is intentionally a working doc—expect to iterate. Leave comments inline in Confluence page linked in linked_artifacts or ping on #hosted-api to schedule a sync.
